The chapter includes older national network and collision figures, historical state crash clocks and costs, and an undated statement that the highway system is only about a century old. These statistical values need current primary-source verification before being served as present-day facts. The vehicles list wrongly includes pedestrians, and the full-access definition and highway-program date wording are ambiguous; neither questionable classification nor an inferred correction is taught. Clear operational rules and definitions remain tied to their cited pages. [A01] [A02] [A03] [A04] [A05]
Memory cue, authored product policy: “People, vehicles, roads”. The cue retrieves complete cited rules and does not replace their conditions.
Terminology: The system combines road users, vehicles and roads; traction means tire grip on the roadway, and hydroplaning means skimming on water rather than retaining that grip.
Misconception to correct: Being below a posted speed limit guarantees that the speed is safe; the source also requires considering weather, traffic and driver condition.
